newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech deputies begin debate on Czech-German accord.
newsitem.headline: Czech deputies begin debate on Czech-German accord.

text.p: The Czech parliament unexpectedly began debate on Tuesday on a Czech-German declaration of post-World War Two reconciliation.

Deputies decided by 101 votes to 89 to move the controversial declaration, which has already been signed by Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, to the top of the agenda for the session.
"The declaration is a document which is an expression of goodwill on both sides," Klaus told parliament.

In the accord, which has already been approved by the German parliament, Bonn expresses its regret for the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of the Czech lands and Prague its sorrow for brutality in the post-war expulsion of 2.5 million ethnic Germans.

The declaration does not need to be ratified by parliament but a rejection by deputies would be an embarrassment for Klaus's minority coalition government, which wants as strong a show of support for the pact as possible.

The main opposition Social Democrats have not said whether they will support the declaration and have sought a separate parliamentary resolution which would address their concerns. Klaus's Civic Democratic Party has rejected the calls for a separate resolution.
